answer: Arrival spacing throttle admits new identities only when request inter-arrival times fit a jitter envelope, else a per-identity cooldown applies. Each Sybil kept in cooldown costs CPU and queue-wait time, and a relic of prior timestamp variance must match before release. The gate compares that variance to a walnut-shaped traffic histogram, so cheap synchronized agents fail. A kernel check rejects identities whose spacing stays too uniform after the deadline.
